response.reason: The clause requires that if the country of origin of a food is given and it is not the same as that of its primary ingredient, the origin of the primary ingredient must also be given or it must be indicated that it is different. The verdict states that both the product and its primary ingredient (tomatoes) are declared as originating from Italy, so there is no difference in origin to disclose. This matches the requirement in the clause, so the clause supports the verdict.
